title: Employee Benefit Plan Claims Procedure Under the Employee Retirement Income Security Act
archetype: ERISA benefit claims and appeals notices
source_verification_depth: Complete Supporting Statement A plus package; underlying cited sources not all independently retrieved. Specific corroboration recorded separately.

score_rationale.reproducibility: Detailed transaction table with counts, minutes and role costs; rounded hour displays require exact minute reconstruction.
score_rationale.provenance: MEPS-IC, Form 5500 and agency projections cited; denial/appeal and timing assumptions require fuller validation.
score_rationale.segmentation: Health, short/long disability, pension, other benefits and claim outcomes are distinguished.
score_rationale.labor: Role-specific EBSA loaded rates tied to shared RIA/PRA methodology; source-to-current-rate chain incomplete.
score_rationale.item13: Paper delivery shares, postage and pages modeled; contracted administration instead included in Item 12.
score_rationale.item14: Zero federal cost asserted without workload analysis.
score_rationale.item15: Totals and updating factors supplied; no full quantified driver decomposition.
score_rationale.validation: Administrative and survey populations; behavioral denial/appeal rates and extreme time values less supported.
score_rationale.consistency: Medical denial 8.67 hours conflicts with prose maximum six hours; several outcome labels differ across tables.

labor.third_party_administration: Included in Item 12 hours by agency convention

item15.reason: Population, claims per participant, wages and postage updates

assumptions: 4336356 unique plans = 2765373 health + 214124 disability + 836843 pension + 520016 other.
Transaction counts repeat plan populations; do not sum row respondents.
Displayed .017/.033-hour values represent one/two minutes; use exact minute fractions.

reconstruction_issues: Prose says transaction burden ranges up to six hours, while medical appeal denial uses 8.67 hours.
Agency explicitly puts purchased third-party administration in Item 12 hours; classification differs from the purchased-service convention and needs guidance reconciliation.
Tables 1 and 3 use inconsistent approved/denied/extended labels for some disability transactions.
methods_worth_testing: Separate unique entities, transactions, outcome branches and delivery modes.
Record the agency cost-classification convention independently of economic labor and purchased-service quantities.
